rule: RS-15. Each entry is one limit the syllabus states, with the pattern C-11 scans learner-facing text for. The sentence is the syllabus’s; the pattern is our judgement of what teaching past the limit would look like. Every contract in the subject carries every entry.

must_catch: Draw the marginal social cost curve.
must_allow: External costs fall on third parties.
Social costs are private costs plus external costs.

entries.syllabus_sentence: Demand and supply diagrams relating to market failure are not required.

entries.construct: the legal detail of business structures
entries.pattern: \b(?:un)?limited liability\b|\bmemorandum of association\b|\barticles of association\b|\bdeed of partnership\b|\bpartnership agreement\b|\bsleeping partners?\b|\bcertificate of incorporation\b|\bannual general meeting\b

must_catch: The memorandum of association sets out the company name.
must_allow: Firms in the private sector aim for profit.
Small firms often find it hard to raise finance.

entries.syllabus_sentence: Detailed knowledge of different types of structure of a firm is not required.

must_allow: Total cost is fixed cost plus variable cost.
Average cost falls as output rises.
Mr Shikongo runs a small firm.

entries.construct: the theory of perfect and imperfect competition

must_catch: Under perfect competition firms are price takers.
must_allow: Competitive markets have many firms, so prices tend to be lower.
A monopoly is the only supplier.

entries.syllabus_sentence: The theory of perfect and imperfect competition and diagrams are not required.

must_allow: Total demand in the economy rises when taxes fall.
This is as true as it was.

entries.syllabus_sentence: Aggregate demand and aggregate supply are not required.
